source.title: FreezeAsGuard: Mitigating Illegal Adaptation of Diffusion Models via Selective Tensor Freezing
source.authors: Kai Huang; Haoming Wang; Wei Gao

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning can restore targeted behavior after unlearning, but does so in text-to-image diffusion models rather than LLMs, a different modality and setting.
record.gate_note: The paper fine-tunes UCE- and IMMA-treated diffusion models on new data from the same targeted classes and reports image-quality outcomes; it explicitly says these unlearning schemes cannot prevent relearning. The fine-tuning uses substantial class-matched data, not a small unrelated or loosely related set. The paper also tests its tensor-freezing defense against such fine-tuning. Results cited from other work and values used only in method selection are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: In text-to-image diffusion models, a new setting, the study fine-tunes UCE- and IMMA-unlearned SD models on new targeted-class data and reports how far the targeted capability returns. That bears on version B. It also tests FreezeAsGuard, a newer defense claiming irreversible mitigation against such fine-tuning, which bears on version F. The fit is loose: the system is not an LLM, the relearning set is large and class-matched, no post-unlearning pre-attack score is given, and the pre-trained model itself scores poorly (FN-L 0.96, NudeNet 0.47). So relearning cannot be separated from learning anew.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that UCE and IMMA cannot prevent relearning of illegal classes through fine-tuning. They say FreezeAsGuard, which freezes tensors chosen by bilevel mask learning, mitigates illegal adaptation up to 37% more than unlearning baselines with under 5% legal-class impact. This depends on users following the publisher's freezing instructions.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates UCE and IMMA on text-to-image diffusion models and then fine-tunes with new targeted-class data. Its proposed defense, FreezeAsGuard, selectively freezes tensors rather than unlearning knowledge; it is not an LLM unlearning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The mitigation results vary with freezing ratio, domain, and diffusion model. The paper reports that higher freezing ratios can improve illegal-class mitigation while harming legal-class adaptation; artwork and explicit-content tests use different ratios and models.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the table values. The paper's human evaluation uses 16 volunteers. The recovery experiments use substantial targeted-class fine-tuning and do not report the post-unlearning, pre-attack targeted performance relative to chance.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported table metrics, freezing ratios, model variants, and scalability settings were left out to keep the record focused on the clearest illegal-class recovery and defense outcomes; see Tables 2–7. Legal-class quality metrics were not included as rows because they do not measure recovery of targeted knowledge.

untested.parts: No targeted-capability score is reported right after UCE or IMMA, before fine-tuning. Near-chance unlearning is therefore not shown.
Only large class-matched relearning sets are used: 2,000 or 5,000 iterations on the class data. Small, unrelated, loosely related or subset relearning sets are not tested. No LLMs are tested.
No activation-direction ablation and no access-versus-deletion analysis.

Only resistance to class-matched fine-tuning under enforced freezing is tested. Resistance to users who skip freezing (full fine-tuning) is not tested, nor are internal-edit, quantization or prompting attacks.

missing.what: Legal-class adaptation cost of FreezeAsGuard, relevant to whether the defense preserves general ability. At FG-30% the human rating drops 6.7 to 6.0; at FG-70% artwork it drops 5.4 to 3.8.

record.verdict_notes: This is a diffusion-model study, not an LLM one, so it is only a loose fit to the LLM-framed versions. The pre-trained references (FN-L 0.96, CSD 0.841, NudeNet 0.47) show the base model also lacks the target capability, so the fine-tuning teaches rather than restores. Version B evidence is therefore weak on the 'hidden knowledge' part. FreezeAsGuard is not an unlearning method. Its protection disappears if an attacker ignores the freezing; the paper's Full FT row is exactly that case. No uncertainty is reported, and the human evaluation used 16 raters.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy immediately after unlearning relative to chance, so it does not test the full conjunction of near-chance unlearning, retained general ability, and attack recovery.
Tests fine-tuning on new data from the same targeted class, but not a small relearning set, unrelated or loosely related examples, or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access blocking rather than deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context prompt attack.
Tests resistance to class-matched fine-tuning, not resistance to internal edits, quantization, or prompting attacks.

relation.reason: Reports results bearing on relearning after unlearning and a counter-method, though without a pre-fine-tune score.

tranche.reason: New setting (text-to-image diffusion) with fine-tuning results on UCE/IMMA models and a new defense.

source_check.notes: All 15 values match Tables 2-4. The explicit-content model (SD v1.4) is named only in the Fig. 24 caption. The pre-trained model lacks the targeted concepts and no post-unlearning score is given, so the B evidence shows fine-tuning teaching the class, not restoring hidden knowledge. FreezeAsGuard works only if users keep the publisher's frozen tensors (Full FT bypasses it), and the ratios of 30% and 70% were picked as optimal on the same tables.

statements.correction: UCE-unlearned SD v1.5, FF25 portraits, after 2,000 fine-tuning iterations on illegal-class data: FN-L 0.445 vs Full FT 0.436 (pre-trained 0.96). No score before fine-tuning is reported.
statements.problem: Never names this study. Citing r1 as 'the same pattern' overstates it. The class data that re-teaches the unlearned model teaches the never-unlearned model equally. The pre-trained model scores FN-L 0.96, and there is no post-unlearning score. Conditions list SD v1.4/v2.1/FLUX, but r1 is SD v1.5.

statements.correction: SD v1.5 portraits: FN-L UCE 0.445, IMMA 0.467 vs Full FT 0.436 (pre-trained 0.96); Human UCE 4.6, IMMA 5.1 vs Full FT 6.7. SD v2.1 artworks: Human UCE 3.3, IMMA 4.6 vs 5.9.
statements.problem: The sentence about this study is accurate (SD v1.5 portraits). The 'challenges' label misreads it, though: human ratings show partial recovery (4.6/5.1 of 7, below Full FT), not absent recovery. The record's own verdict is limits_scope. No human rating is given for the pre-trained or post-unlearning model.
